text:
Minh: Heads-up — canary on staging showing 15-25% tail latency regression for our 8-GPU TP + INT8 runs. Pattern: big all-reduce spikes at step boundaries when seq lengths vary a lot.
Sara: saw a couple alerts, didn't dig in yet :eyes:
perf-bot: Profile uploaded: https://perf.redwood/profiles/2030123456 (flamegraph + nvprof timeline)
Tom: quick skim of timeline — NCCL allreduce latency jumps exactly when rank ordering diverges. looks like rank skew from KV cache misses (some ranks processing longer contexts)
Minh: yep. two addtl things I noticed from the trace:
```
[step 124] rank0 compute 14ms | allreduce wait 42ms
[step 124] rank3 compute 8ms  | allreduce wait 60ms
kernel_selector: selected=fp32_gemm fallback_reason=scale_overflow layer=12 shape=(2048,2048) scale=35.2
```
So one layer fell back to FP32 (slower) because quant scale exceeded saturation threshold — that pushes compute on some ranks and amplifies comm skew.
Rachel: that fallback is nasty. we previously saw per-tensor quant clipping problems. can we do per-channel or clamp earlier?
Minh: short-term patch I tried locally: clamp scale at prequantize stage and prefer int8 kernel if shape dims >= 1024. Patch snippet:
```
// kernel_selector.cc
if (shape[0] >= 1024 && scale < MAX_CLAMP) {
  choose(INT8_FUSED_GEMM);
} else if (scale >= MAX_CLAMP) {
  scale = MAX_CLAMP; // clamp to avoid fallback
}
```
Sara: can we A/B this in canary with an env toggle? REDWOOD_FORCE_INT8=1 maybe
infra-bot: Canary deployment triggered: canary/8gpu-dedicated, env REDWOOD_FORCE_INT8=1, build=2026.03.17-87
Tom: also try NCCL tuning: set NCCL_ALGO=ring and NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVL for the test, sometimes tree algorithm has weird spikes for these tensor sizes.
Rachel: another mitigation is batching heuristics — bucket short sequences to 16/32 token bins to reduce variance across ranks. padding is tradeoff but reduces skew.
Minh: test results after 30m: tail latency dropped ~9% (p95->p95.9) with the forced-int8 + clamp + padding. p50 unchanged. still seeing residual allreduce jitter for tensors <64KB.
Tom: for smaller tensors, we should try allreduce chunking adjustments and earlier overlap: kick off async allreduce as soon as layer output ready (non-blocking) rather than wait for full backward pass accumulation.
Sara: agree. action items?
Minh: I'll open two PRs: (1) smarter kernel selector that considers runtime skew metric + clamp on prequantize, (2) small-allreduce path that prioritizes async overlap and uses NCCL comm streams. I'll add an opt-in config so Dedicated customers can enable aggressive int8.
Rachel: I'll add a short eval (prompt set) to track quality drift from clamping vs per-channel quant to make sure we don't regress generation quality.
Tom: I'll run cluster-wide perf sweep for different NCCL_ALGO/P2P combos and collect histograms.
Sara: nice. if anyone needs me to triage canary alerts ping me. :thumbsup:
Minh: thanks all. this is probably the main cause of recent production noise — interplay of KV cache misses -> variable seq len -> compute skew -> int8 fallback -> allreduce spikes. Will keep thread updated with PR links.
perf-bot: Saved profile snapshot -> /profiles/2030123456/snapshot-1
infra-bot: Canary finished (30m). Metrics: p95 -9%, p99 -4%, cost delta ~+0.2% due to padding. Logs archived.
Sara: :+1:
